range: Southern Serengeti plains to the Masai Mara, through the western corridor.
distance: On the order of 800 km from the southern plains to the Mara. The circuit changes from year to year.
timing: Calving on the short-grass plains from January to March. North through the western corridor by June. On the Mara in the dry season. South again with the short rains in November.
summary: The Serengeti–Mara herds walk a rough circle after rain and fresh grass. River crossings at the Grumeti and the Mara are the dangerous days. This line is a representative seasonal round, not a tracked herd.
uncertaintyNote: Monthly positions are a literature sketch of the seasonal round. They are not the 1999–2000 GPS tracks. Every point is representative or interpolated, and approximate.

events.label: Calving
events.text: Calves are born on the southern short-grass plains, roughly January to March.

events.label: Grumeti
events.text: Herds cross the Grumeti on the way north. The exact crossing shifts with the rain.

events.label: Mara River
events.text: The Mara crossing, in the dry season, is the best-known hazard on the circuit.

events.label: Short rains
events.text: When the short rains reach the south, the herds leave the Mara.

provenance.source: Thirgood, S. et al. 2004. Can parks protect migratory ungulates? The case of the Serengeti wildebeest. Animal Conservation 7:113–120.
